slides.title: How it works
slides.html: OpenDefence Matrix puts your OpenDefence chat under the ATAK map, in the same chats as Element X. Positions and map items in messages go on your map with a tap.

slides.title: Your account
slides.html: Your chat account is your OpenDefence account on Matrix, the chat system Element X also uses. Your rooms and messages are the same in both apps.

slides.title: Signing in
slides.html: Once the Deploy App has connected ATAK to your OpenDefence TAK server, you sign in on each phone with your Deploy App certificate. There is no server to type in.

slides.title: Recovery key
slides.html: Your first device gives you a recovery key to keep safe. A later phone reads encrypted messages only after you verify it with that key or another of your devices.

slides.title: Rooms and direct chats
slides.html: A room is a group chat, such as your platoon's, and a direct chat is between you and one person. Chats lists both.

slides.title: Your OpenDefence space
slides.html: Your OpenDefence space groups the rooms its members can join. A room you make goes there, and others see it in Chats under MORE ROOMS IN, with Join.

slides.title: Room admins
slides.html: Whoever makes a room is its Admin. In Room info the admin can rename it, invite people and give roles.

slides.title: Threads
slides.html: A thread keeps a side conversation under one message, so it does not flood the room. The room shows only how many replies it has.

slides.title: Writing with no connection
slides.html: Chats says when you are offline, but you can still read and write. A new message waits as Sending… and goes by itself, so do not send it again.

slides.title: Chat and the map
slides.html: Messages carry positions, map items and map files as well as words, and a tap shows them on your map. Live locations shared in Element X appear with no tap.

slides.title: Positions on messages
slides.html: In encrypted chats your position goes with each message by default, as the grid under it. The pin by the message field turns that off for a chat.

slides.title: Map items
slides.html: Points, routes and drawings travel through chats as MAP ITEM cards. One goes on your map only when you tap On map, and is not passed on to anyone.

slides.title: Map files
slides.html: Route and area files (KML, KMZ or GPX) can go on your map as an overlay you can hide. As with map items, only your tap puts them there.

slides.title: Live locations
slides.html: People who share their live location in Element X, in a chat you are in, show on your map by name without a tap.

slides.title: Notifications
slides.html: By default ATAK notifies you of direct messages and of messages that name you, called mentions. OD Matrix Preferences in ATAK's Settings changes that for this phone.

slides.title: No text in notifications
slides.html: A notification names the chat and how many messages are new, never the text, because ATAK shows notifications on a locked screen.

slides.title: Unread count
slides.html: The chat button in ATAK's toolbar and Chat on OpenDefence Main's thumb bar count every unread message, whatever notifications you choose.
